valuation.method: Forward non-GAAP EPS x P/E, with FY2027 non-GAAP diluted EPS used as the forward earnings base at the 12-month target date (Nov 2027). FY2026E non-GAAP EPS is built from the Q3 FY2026 release: nine-month non-GAAP EPS $2.87 plus Q4 of about $1.03 (Q4 guided non-GAAP operating margin 32% on about $4.35B revenue, about 1.05B diluted shares) gives about $3.90; the company does not guide EPS. FY2027 EPS = $3.90 x (1 + growth), growth 12% bear, 18% base, 24% bull, against FY2026 subscription revenue guidance of $15.78-15.79B (+22.5%, +21% constant currency) that includes Armis. Targets are per share of the NYSE listing in USD, after the 5-for-1 split; no ADR or FX conversion applies.

bear.driver: Seat-based workflow demand weakens against AI agents, growth decelerates toward low teens and the multiple compresses to a mature-software level

base.driver: Subscription growth slows to high teens as guided cRPO growth (18.5% constant currency in Q4) implies, with margin about 32% and AI ACV ($1.7B target) adding growth

bull.driver: AI Control Tower and Now Assist monetization re-accelerates growth and margins, restoring a premium software multiple

valuation.implied_by_close: At FY2026E EPS of $3.90 the close of $102.25 implies 26.2x; at base FY2027 EPS of $4.60 it implies 22.2x. The four named post-earnings targets average $169 (range $110-$201) but none has a documented 12-month horizon, so no weighted target is formed; the $169 average implies about 36.8x base FY2027 EPS, or EPS of $7.04 at 24x.
valuation.sensitivity: One turn of P/E moves the base target by $4.60 (about 4.2 pp of the $110 base). A 2-point change in FY2027 EPS growth moves base EPS by about $0.08 and the base target by about $1.9 at 24x.
valuation.watch_metric: Subscription revenue growth and cRPO growth in constant currency (Q4 guide 18.5% cRPO), together with non-GAAP operating margin against the 32% Q4 guide and any AI ACV progress against the $1.7B target.
valuation.next_disclosure: Q4 and full-year FY2026 results with FY2027 guidance, expected around late January 2027; the date is not confirmed in the sources found.

analyst_notes: Four named calls were dated 29 October 2026, the day after the Q3 release: Baird $185, Cantor $201 and BofA $180 (all Buy) and KeyBanc Sell at $110. Prior targets were not stated in the source, so revisions cannot be measured. The stock was about $150 before the print and fell roughly 19% in extended trading, then drifted to $102.25 by 13 November, so every Buy target sat 76-97% above the close and several are likely stale. The gap to the $110 base case is mostly multiple: $180 needs about 39x base FY2027 EPS, or EPS near $7.50 at 24x. Only KeyBanc's target is near the close.
